  • Binary protocol for point cloud type input and output

Binary protocol for point cloud type input and output

What does it do (one sentence)

Points/XYZPoints/NormalPoints/RGBPoints These port types, whether used as node input or output, transmit not ordinary JSON, but a customized compact binary format. Runtime Single-node direct operation will try to automatically process .ply paths and encoded bytes according to node port types; Python SDK also exposes the three functions encode_point_cloud_payload / load_ply_points / decode_point_cloud_payload to facilitate you to manually process this format.

This is not the point cloud format in normal mode RuntimeFrame. Normal mode RuntimeFrame.point_cloud uses another simpler format: [height, width, 3] reshape float32 original array, without the protocol header mentioned below. Passive binocular passive_bino mode transmits EPICRAW3, and does not transmit individually point_cloud. The two cannot be mixed, see Runtime input frames (RuntimeFrame / RuntimePassiveBinoFrame) for details.

Why is there this mechanism?

The amount of point cloud data is usually very large (tens of thousands to millions of points), and the overhead of using JSON for transmission and analysis is too high. The server has agreed on a compact float32 binary format. At the same time, considering that a port sometimes carries multiple point clouds at a time, the format contains the header information of "number of point clouds + length of each part" to facilitate one-time segmentation by the server.

How does it affect your development

When passing a value to the point cloud type input (for example SingleNodeParams(…​, inputs={"points": …​})), it is recommended to directly pass the local .ply path; SDK will automatically encode it into the format required by the protocol according to the node input port type:

from atom_sdk import SingleNodeParams

result = client.runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(
    SingleNodeParams("EstimateNormal", inputs={"points": "/data/scan.ply"})
)

If you already have a point array in hand, or need to explicitly control the point dimensions, you can also manually code:

from atom_sdk import SingleNodeParams, encode_point_cloud_payload, load_ply_points

points = load_ply_points("/data/scan.ply")           # from PLY File read flattened xyz float list
payload = encode_point_cloud_payload(points, point_dim=3)  # Encoded into the binary format required by the protocol

result = client.runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(
    SingleNodeParams("EstimateNormal", inputs={"points": payload})
)

When reading point cloud type output from the server, most interfaces SDK will automatically parse it for you (such as get_binded_point_cloud_parsed), and you do not need to care about this layer of protocol. But run_single_node_no_graph is an exception to the following nodes - they directly return unencapsulated raw point cloud bytes (bytes), and you need to call decode_point_cloud_payload yourself to parse:

  • CalculateEdge

  • CalculateEdgeNew

  • EstimateNormal

  • DownSample

  • DownSampleWithNormal

  • FilterByNormal

from atom_sdk import decode_point_cloud_payload

result = client.runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(
    SingleNodeParams("EstimateNormal", inputs={"points": payload})
)
# result Yes bytes,No dict —— This is the fixed behavior of the above nodes
clouds = decode_point_cloud_payload(result, has_dim_in_header=False, point_dim=6)
print(clouds[0].shape)          # (Points, 6)  -> [x, y, z, nx, ny, nz]
print(clouds[0].tolist()[:2])

point_dim should be determined according to the actual type of the node output port: XYZPoints/Points is passed to 3; NormalPoints (with normal vector)/RGBPoints (with color) is passed to 6. For details, see dtype in outputs_info in the node definition.

When you might encounter problems

  1. SDK cannot find the node input type, or use the old version SDK: In this case, inputs={"points": "/data/scan.ply"} may be uploaded as an ordinary file, and the PLY file content will be passed to the server as it is. When the server presses float32 to parse, it will report AtomApiError: buffer size must be a multiple of element size.
    Solution: Upgrade SDK, or use input_data_types={"points": "XYZPoints"} to explicitly tell SDK the port type; Python can also use load_ply_points + encode_point_cloud_payload to manually encode and then transmit.

  2. Thought run_single_node_no_graph must return dict: For the special nodes listed above, the return value is bytes, and directly result["xxx"] will report TypeError: byte indices must be integers.
    Solution: Determine the type first, or know in advance which node you are adjusting, process it directly with bytes, and use decode_point_cloud_payload to parse.

  3. point_dim Transmission error: Parsing the output with normal vector according to point_dim=3 will cause data misalignment after reshape (each line will mistake the coordinates of the next point as the field of the current point).
    Solution: Check the node’s outputs_info to confirm whether the port’s dtype is XYZPoints (3) or NormalPoints/RGBPoints (6).

How to deal with problems

  1. Prioritize directly passing the .ply path and let SDK automatically encode according to the node port type; if the node type cannot be automatically queried, then explicitly pass input_data_types, or use load_ply_points + encode_point_cloud_payload to manually generate bytes in Python.

  2. Before calling run_single_node_no_graph, confirm whether the node name is in the special list above; if so, expect to get bytes in advance.

  3. After getting bytes, use decode_point_cloud_payload(raw, has_dim_in_header=False, point_dim=…​) to parse. has_dim_in_header always passes False in this scenario.

technical details

The essence of the protocol is an array of float32, arranged in little endian order:

[cloud_count, size_0, size_1, ..., size_{cloud_count-1}, data_0..., data_1..., ...]
Field Description

cloud_count

carried several point clouds this time. In the SingleNodeParams scenario, it is usually 1

size_i The total number of flattened floating points of

th i point cloud (points × point_dim, not bytes)

data_i

The original data of the i point cloud, arranged continuously in groups of point_dim

decode_point_cloud_payload(payload, *, has_dim_in_header, point_dim=None)：

Parameter Type Description

payload

bytes

Raw binary point cloud stream

has_dim_in_header

bool

Whether the header information contains additional dimensions of each point cloud; run_single_node_no_graph’s special node scene is fixedly transmitted `False

point_dim

int or None

When the header information does not have dimensions, manually specify the dimensions of each point for reshape

Returns list[ParsedPointCloud], ParsedPointCloud.values is the flattened array('f'), .shape is the recommended shape, .tolist() is converted to a nested list by shape.

encode_point_cloud_payload(points, *, point_dim=3)：

Parameter Type Description

points

flattened floating-point sequence, or row-wise point sequence (such as [(x,y,z), …​])

will be automatically flattened, and the two writing methods are equivalent.

point_dim

int

Number of channels per point: xyz uses 3, with normal vector/color uses 6

load_ply_points(path, *, properties=("x", "y", "z"))：

Parameter Type Description

path

File path

PLY files, automatically recognize ascii/binary_little_endian/binary_big_endian

properties

tuple[str, …​]

The vertex attribute name to be extracted, flattened in order; the normal vector can be passed ("x","y","z","nx","ny","nz")

Only the attributes declared in the vertex element will be parsed, and other element such as face, camera, etc. will be automatically skipped.
